Episode 247. Liberation War of Laprarosa (16)
Shimat's wavering sword gradually became calm. His inner turmoil, bound by deep contemplation, was finding its way back once more.
The price for his sins was already set.
As Luna said, there was no need to drag it into this fight.
"To spare a capable opponent, you're becoming more like the Blue Wind Emperor."
Shimat shrugged his shoulders as he spoke. Even amidst a sense of defeat, strangely, he didn't feel unpleasant or humiliation.
Despite the eternal pain awaiting him regardless of victory or defeat, he oddly felt a sense of enjoyment.

"As I reached enlightenment, I could see more clearly. There was, after all, a significant gap between the Blue Wind Emperor, that old man, and me. But essentially, I was confident that I was stronger than him."
"Because you treated your enemies more cruelly?"
"Yes. I couldn't understand how he entered this realm, even stronger than me, back then. But now... I understand. Genesis is just one stage among many."
Luna nodded as if agreeing.
"What one carries, in some aspects, is more important than the stage itself. In that sense, my attainment, driven only by desire for myself and my kin, is merely pathetic."
Shhhhh...!
Shimat's sword thrust forward. As if the distance between them had been an illusion, the blade suddenly flew towards Luna's face.
Luna smoothly turned her body. Krantel rotated with her, creating a heavy sword wind, but Shimat didn't dodge and thrust his sword again.
His purple blade rushed towards Luna's heart. Luna deflected it with Krantel's hilt, then used the recoil to push Shimat away.
"Pathetic, yet dangerous."
Contrary to her words, Luna was finding a strange sense of ease.
A new sensation was coming to her. Something deep inside seemed to be stirring, causing her heart to swell with an inexplicable thrill.
'It's becoming clearer.'
The direction of Shimat's blade, the spreading of his purple aura, the fine line between life and death marked by a step, a breath - all were deepening.
Even as Shimat's blade grazed her neck, passed by her face. No longer did Luna feel a chilling sensation.
Instead, she boldly closed the distance between them. White aura and purple energy mingled like mist.
The metal inside the hull, caught in the mist, disintegrated into fine powder. The softly clashing energies expanded their territory, circling around them.
The more this happened, the further Luna moved from her familiar ways. Swinging her sword destructively, wildly releasing energy, charging fiercely.
But she hadn't forgotten.
Luna was merely biding her time. Harmoniously fighting with Shimat as if in sync, she planned to explode in a moment.
She was just beginning to feel a new power surging within her. That power, pulsing like a giant heart, was ready to burst out at any moment.
Shimat precisely read her intention.
But he had no thoughts of avoiding it. He planned to face Luna's new power head-on.
It was a courtesy to his opponent, who had come risking her life, to himself, who would soon perish even if left alone.
It was the final fight of a long, dark life that had spanned forever.
Like the times he had been abandoned, without clan, without air fortresses or kin, fighting utterly alone, Shimat was fully committing himself.
'Come, Luna Runkandel. Show me what you have. Perhaps another essence of the Blue Wind Emperor that I am unaware of...'
Shimat kept thinking about Eltiot. He was anticipating the sword style inherited by Luna.
'That sword will be beautiful. Even to these eyes of Shimat, who knew only of slaughter and conquest.'
Thud! Fzzzzzt...!

Suddenly, the hull tilted. The aftermath of the Plutonian Domination Swords falling from the outside had collapsed Kri. The part of the hull where Luna and Shimat stood was splitting like a glacier and plummeting to the ground.
Jin's energy flowed through the cracks of the hull. Golden lightning rapidly formed golden waterfalls inside.
As if on cue.
Both leaped towards each other simultaneously. Shimat attacked with a thrust, while Luna swung Krantel from a distance.
'It seems slower, but it's not.'
Shimat anticipated Krantel's acceleration just before the collision.
'And she plans to slice me along with the sword? No... that's not the Blue Wind Emperor’s style.'
So, what was Luna's newly attained realm? For a moment, that question filled Shimat's mind.
Between what is visible and what is not.
Before the swords made contact, one had to discover what was hidden in the gap. However, even the insight of Genesis made it challenging to capture everything in that brief moment.
'The acceleration is certain. The sword Luna Runkandel will wield after accelerating, no, it wasn't acceleration! It was the Sword of Light...!'

The 'Sword of Light' was a technique Eltiot prepared during his prime for Shimat. It was meant to be used after Shimat, who was neither Red Plutonian nor Blue Plutonian, had awakened to the principle of harmony.
However, Shimat had left Eltiot before the Sword of Light was completed and had since forgotten about it.
As vivid as yesterday, the form of the Sword of Light began to emerge in his mind. Eltiet must have completed this unfinished technique for Luna.
'There couldn't be a more fitting sword to cut me down.'
The Sword of Light Shimat remembered was a straightforward sword, fitting its grandiose name. A direct sword without sudden acceleration or tricky changes in trajectory.
Krantel was approaching at its initial speed. In this state, Shimat's sword would inevitably touch first.
However, at the moment the swords were about to clash, Shimat's vision was suddenly tinged with red.
The unique red aura of the mind sword, but deeper than that. Shimat had never seen this crimson energy before, now entwining Krantel.
As Shimat had predicted, Krantel did not accelerate.
Instead, it moved as if 'erasing' space, just like Shimat had shown earlier, completely shattering his calculation in an instant.
I am not your master, Shimat.
The crimson blade spoke as such. This was not the sword of the Blue Wind Emperor but the sword of Runkandel, the White Whale.
The power that had begun to resonate within her from the moment she shook off the temptation of the red energy. Luna knew that Shimat kept projecting Eltiot onto her.
Thud...!
Shimat's sword pierced Luna's chest.
But the blade did not penetrate as deeply as he had intended. Although it was brief, it was the price of being entangled in the past.
He had continually faced the past through Luna, while Luna had only looked towards the future of this fight.
The power to change fate.
Even with the power of Genesis, one cannot change a fate long passed.
And even without the power of Genesis, sometimes people can transcend fate. Just as Luna was now delivering a fatal blow to Shimat, surpassing the gap between them.
An impossible event was unfolding, considering only the martial prowess of the two.
Shimat's sword cut shallowly, while Luna's sword cut deeply. Krantel grazed Shimat's neck, deeply entered his chest, and then struck down the left side of his heart of light.
Crash!
A loud sound and vibration as one side of the red luminous heart shattered, sending sharp fragments flying. Thick, heavy blood-like red energy poured out of the cracks.
It was Luna's groan. Shimat had exploded the red energy in the wound as he retreated. Luna, gritting her teeth, pursued Shimat, trying to widen the distance.
Despite her severe injury, her body did not feel heavy.

Luna was sensing it. The impending transcendence. All the experiences and insights she accumulated as the first generation of the family, as a member of the Black Sea Expedition, and as Eltiat's disciple were explosively erupting.
She wanted to keep swinging Krantel non-stop, embedding all that into it. Doing so, she felt like she could erase not only Shimat but the entire Great Desert from the map in an instant.
'Harmony.'
But Luna did not hastily grasp at the transcendent moment now within reach.
She needed to finely tune and embrace everything so that all could shine together, nothing omitted or buried.
'It's not just an evolution of the red power, but a magic sword.'
Along with the crimson energy, a calm magical wind arose around her. Luna stepped forward on this magic as if it were a path.
Even though her speed wasn't fast, Shimat couldn't easily escape. In front, the crimson energy, and behind, the magic, were constricting him.
The fragments of the heart of light crumbled between the crimson energy and the magic. Finally, the Red Plutonian Battle God was facing his end.
[Kid, indeed, Rokia's curse is weakening.]

Between Laprarosa and the Human World, in the dimensional rift. The interior was as transparent as a crystal cave. The images of Jin and Murakan reflected on the dimensional wall blurred and then became clear repeatedly.
[Yeah, but it hasn't completely disappeared. It seems there's a problem because Brother Ban is enduring both the curse and the dimensional errors.]
Despite their casual conversation, both were feeling the constant pressure of the encroaching dimensional storm.
A massive current of e;ectric waves flowed inside the dimension. The electric wave from Laprarosa and the one extending from Jin were continually getting closer.
[Hmm, if the pressure is this much at the dimensional gateway to Laprarosa, I'm worried if that guy's liberation device can withstand it. Well, that guy Ban must be guarding it well, right?]
Jin smirked and nodded.
[I can do that too, Murakan. Ban wouldn't fail. But let's speed up a bit more; even if Ban is strong, it's not good for us to be late.]
